newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt issuance to ease afore Veterans Day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt issuance to ease afore Veterans Day.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity is expected to wind down ahead of Monday's holiday but a few names are in the market, dealers said.
"Activity should slow as players head out early for the holiday but we may still see some business today," said one syndicate source.
BellSouth Capital Funding is expected to issue $300 million in 30-year debt with a put option in the fifth and tenth year via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, sources said.
Issuance is expected to remain thin as players head out early ahead of Monday's U.S. Veteran's Day holiday.
The Public Securities Association (PSA) recommends a full close for U.S. credit markets on Monday, in observance of the Veterans Day holiday.
The PSA has also recommended an early, 1400 EST/1900 GMT close for U.S. fixed-income markets on Friday.
Meanwhile, the calendar for private placement debt offerings continues to build, syndicate sources said.
Allied Waste is expected to price $475 million in 144A senior subordinated notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
WCI Steel may also price $300 million in 10-year senior secured notes via Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Securities.
In other issues, Anheuser-Busch is expected to price $250 million in 10-year debt via Dillon Read & Co as early as Friday, sources said. Price talk on the issue is in the 50 to 55 basis points arena.
Looking ahead, a pile of 144A debt offerings are expected to fill the new issue calendar, dealers said.
Cable Plus Holdings is expected to tap the market with $150 million in 144A notes due 2006.
Amtrol Inc may price $115 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006, sources added.
Celestica International may price $150 million in 144A senior subordinated guaranteed notes.
Cole National Corp is expected to price $140 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via CIBC Wood Gundy.
IMED Corp is expected to price $175 million 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities.
Dollar Financial and Peterson Publishing and Atrium Cos are all expected to bring $100 million each in 144A debt offerings near-term, dealers added.
